messages:
Rachel Kim: Hey team — before Marketing starts asking for reference calls + public case studies, can we sanity-check who’s actually “healthy” enough right now? Looking for:
1) any recent escalations we should avoid stepping on
2) preferred customer contacts (who to ask vs who NOT to surprise)
3) any accounts that are a hard no for Q4 references

Miguel Santos: +1. I can pull quick notes from CSMs but off the top:
- Northwind Commerce: generally happy, BUT had that p95 latency spike last week during interview window. Resolved, but would avoid quoting hard numbers until we’re confident it’s stable.
- Helios Health: strong relationship, super cautious on approvals. Not a “no” but needs slow + formal process.
- Cascade Customer Support: please tread carefully. They’re stable now but had an escalation recently (support load + reliability questions). Good for private reference calls *maybe*, not for public story.

Tyler Benson: For tracking — reminder we need to keep DNC (do-not-contact) + health signals in the candidate sheet + HubSpot. If we greenlight anyone, I’ll add a “Reference-Eligible” property + owner so we don’t spam.

Camila Reyes: This is super helpful. For the reference program we can separate:
- reference calls (private) vs
- public assets (logo/quotes/metrics)
So a customer can be eligible for one and not the other.

Rachel Kim: Agree. CS POV: “healthy” = no open Sev1/Sev2 incidents, no unresolved billing/escalation threads, and the exec sponsor is still engaged.
Also: no surprise asks. We need the CSM to pre-brief the champion first.

Avery Johnson: On Northwind — champion is Dana (VP Eng). She’s friendly but hates being pinged last-minute. If we do reference calls, we should batch requests and give her a couple windows.
Also, the ML Lead (Priya) is the best technical voice for prospects.

Miguel Santos: Northwind contacts:
- Dana (VP Eng) = approval path + final sign-off
- Priya (ML Lead) = technical + architecture + “why Redwood”
- Their PM (Lena) = good for outcomes / business framing but less comfortable with numbers
If we ask Dana directly for “metrics” she’ll likely push back unless we offer ranges.

Isabelle Laurent: Re: “recent escalations” — I saw SUP-3812 (Northwind) linked in Jira. Not catastrophic but it’s in the paper trail. If we publish, we should avoid: “X ms p95 guaranteed” language. Ranges + disclaimers are safer.

Camila Reyes: Makes sense. We can focus Northwind story on Dedicated capacity + fallback routing + operational controls, and keep metrics as ranges / before-after % when approved.

Rachel Kim: Cascade:
- They’re a good reference-call candidate *only* if we control the agenda.
- Please avoid any prospect lines of questioning around: “Why did you have downtime in August?” (they’ll bring up old pain).
- Preferred contact is Morgan (Head of Support Ops). Do NOT loop in their CTO unless CSM preps him.

Miguel Santos: +1 on Cascade. Their escalation was mostly about response times + expectations setting. They’re sensitive to “marketing-y” asks.
If we do calls, I’d cap to 1/month and add explicit opt-out / cooldown.

Tyler Benson: Operationally we can enforce a cooldown: after a reference call, auto-set “Cooldown until” = +30 days. I can set a task/automation reminder, but we need agreement on policy.

Rachel Kim: I like 30 days default, with CSM override.
Also request lead time: minimum 7 business days unless it’s a truly critical deal.

Avery Johnson: For Atlas Insurance: they’re not a “healthy reference” yet. Procurement + SLA negotiation is still touchy. If we ask too early it could backfire.
Maybe keep them as a *future* reference once the support/SLA terms are signed.

Miguel Santos: Polaris DevTools: they’re happy and fast-moving. Low risk for reference calls. Public logo/metrics: maybe, but they’ll want to move quickly and keep it dev-focused.
Preferred contact: Rohan (Head of Eng). He loves talking DX + time-to-value.

Camila Reyes: Great. So tentative buckets:
- Green (calls + potential public): Polaris
- Yellow (calls yes, public TBD w/ caveats): Northwind
- Yellow/Red (calls maybe, public no): Cascade
- Red (not yet): Atlas
- Helios: special handling (public possible but slow + constrained)
Does that match CS view?

Rachel Kim: Yes, with Helios nuance:
- Helios is “healthy” relationship-wise, but they’re compliance-first.
- Preferred contact is Hannah (Compliance PM) for what can be said publicly, and their Security lead (Arjun) for technical validation.
- If we go public, expect multiple review rounds and anonymization requests.

Isabelle Laurent: If we tag deals influenced by references, please make sure Sales logs:
- “Reference Call Used = Yes/No”
- which customer
- date
Otherwise we can’t measure program impact.

Tyler Benson: I’ll update the intake checklist to require:
- CSM approval
- AE approval
- customer contact + preferred times
- topics to avoid
- whether public logo/quote is in-scope

Camila Reyes: Perfect. Rachel/Miguel — can you drop any other “hard no” accounts we should avoid this month?

Rachel Kim: Hard no for Oct:
- anyone with open Sev1/Sev2 or active escalation thread
- Aurora Payments (for now) — they’re evaluating, but their uptime/regional constraints are still a sore spot. Not the moment to ask.

Miguel Santos: Co-sign Aurora as “not yet.” They have the right story but we need to earn stability trust first.

Rachel Kim: Cool. Action items:
- Tyler to encode cooldown + lead time expectations in the intake flow
- Camila to align buckets in the candidate list
- Miguel to confirm preferred contacts + “avoid list” per account w/ the CSMs

Camila Reyes: :thumbsup: Thanks all — this helps a lot.

Tyler Benson: :thumbsup: Will share an updated checklist in #announcements once it’s ready.

Isabelle Laurent: +1 and pls @ me when HubSpot properties change so reporting doesn’t break.
